FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 28 April, 1989, after the draft finalized by the Sports Goods Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Division Council. This standard was first issued in 1965. It has now been revised to take into account of the comments received on the standard from time to time. References in the standard have also been updated. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard
SPORTS NETS SPECIFICATION

( First Revision )
1 SCOPE This standard covers requirements for nets for lawn tennis, badminton, table tennis, volleyball, tenikoit, basketball, cricket practice, football goals and hockey goals. 2 REFERENCES

4 REQUIREMENTS 4.1 The nets shall meet the requirements Table 1.

Specification for steel wire engineering ropes for general purposes ( second revision )

3 MATERIALS

3.1 The nets shall be manufactured from cord made of good quality cotton yarn of 60 tex ( 10 s ), 60 tex x 2 ( 10 s/2 ) or 60 tex x 3 ( 10 s/3 ) soft hemp or polyethylene, as required by the purchaser. 3.2 The rope used with nets shall be made from good quality cotton yarn of 60 tex ( 10 s ) or manila or polyethylene or nylon, as required by the purchaser. 3.3 The wire rope for use with lawn tennis nets shall be of 8 mm diameter conforming to any construction of 1s 2266 : 1977. 3.4 The material for the hems for shall be as given below:
Net

4.2 The tape of the material specified in 3.4 shall be doubled over the edge of the net and stitched properly. The width of the hem after stitching shall be as given in Table 1. The nets for lawn tennis and badminton shall be hemmed at the top only. The nets for volleyball, tenikoit and table tennis shall be hemmed both on top and bottom edges. 4.3 The knots in the netting shall grip properly and shall not jump back or slip during use. 4.4 The colours of different nets shall be as shown in Table 1. It shall be of uniform shade and shall not fade during the reasonable life of the nets. 4.5 Side Bands for Volleyball Nets Tapes of white material, 50 mm wide and 1 m long shall be fastened, one on each side of the net perpendicular to the intersection of the respective side line and to the axis of the central line. Both side bands shall be considered as part of the net. 4.6 Antennas for Volleyball Nets The antennas shall be flexible rods made of fibre glass or similar material, 1'80 m long and 10 mm in diameter. The antennas shall be marked with 100 mm bands of contrasting colours, preferably red and white. One antenna each is fastened on to the outer edge of each vertical side band extending 0'80 m above the top of the net. They are considered part of the net and mark its side limits. 1

IS 3345 : 1989 5 MARKING 5.1 Each net shall be marked at a suitable place with the manufacturer's name, trade-mark or identification mark and the material used in its manufacture; or a label showing these particulars shall be attached to the net. 6 PACKING The nets shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 7 SAMPLING 7.1 Lot In any consignment, all the nets of one type, manufactured from the same material and belonging to the same batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot. 7.1.1 Each lot shall be tested separately to ascertain its conformity to the requirements of this standard. 7.2 To ascertain the conformity of the lot to the requirements of this standard, the number of nets to be selected at random shall be in accordance with co1 1 and 2 of Table 2. Table 2 Sample Size and Criteria for Conformity ( CIauses 7.2 and 7.3.2 )

7.3 Number of Tests and Criteria for Conformity 7.3.1 The nets selected according to 7.2 shall be inspected for all the applicable requirements given in 4 and Table 1 7.3.2 The lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of this standard if the number of defective nets, that is those failing in one or more of the requirements, does not exceed the corresponding acceptance number given in co1 3 of Table 2.

Standard Mark

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the &reau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Bureau of Iadian Staudards

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending. to connected matters in the country.
